clue.text: The wake of the fart knocked over mother

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit over, covering, the word for mother placed inside them
knocked about, the letters of the fart are battered into a new order

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A schoolboy joke: someone breaks wind so violently that their mother is bowled over in its trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked' shuffles THE FART into AFTERTH, and 'over' wraps it round MA, splitting it as AFTER-MA-TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in the wake of something means in its aftermath, the period of consequences following an event.

clue.text: Stockpile caps for any modern US gas outlet?

indicators.note: caps are tops, so the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: in American slang the backside is the ass, the outlet for gas

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about hoarding tops for some up-to-date American petrol station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas outlet' looks like a petrol pump in American English; it is the rear end, 'US' signalling the American spelling ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stockpile is to gather and accumulate a large store of something.

clue.text: Locum work is alluring, but only half the time

indicators.note: but only signals that the word is kept short of something, one piece taken away

parts.note: something alluring is tempting
the synonym holds two Ts, each an abbreviation for time; half of that pair is one T

explanation.surface: Someone finds stand-in jobs appealing, but only some of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: T abbreviates time; the synonym has two of them, and 'half the time' is one of that pair, removed under 'but only'.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum fills in for an absent doctor or professional, which is temporary work, or temping.

clue.text: Split with Hoskins over sex (no upward performance)

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart or split
the setter Hoskins refers to himself as I

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for sex reads backwards

parts.note: IT is a coy old word for sex

indicators.note: in a down clue upward means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: The setter splits from a partner, complaining that sex no longer gets going upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IT into TI, and 'upward' turns NO into ON in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rendition is an interpretation or performance of a piece of music or drama.

clue.text: An order ignored by some musicians who played on?

definitions.text: An order ignored by some musicians who played on?

parts.words: An order ignored by some musicians who played on?
parts.note: the Titanic's band famously kept playing as the ship sank, ignoring the order to leave the vessel

explanation.surface: Musicians carry on playing despite being told to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The bandsmen of the Titanic are said to have played on as it went down; the answer also splits as A BAND ON SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain's command to evacuate a sinking vessel is the order the Titanic's musicians disregarded.

clue.text: Detest not going all the way in Balmoral?

indicators.note: the word stops short of its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to detest is to hate

explanation.surface: A royal hates something at the Scottish castle, though not wholeheartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral looks like the royal castle, but a balmoral is also a Scottish brimless bonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a balmoral is a type of flat Scottish cap, a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Forbidden love old club brought back

indicators.note: brought back means the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: An affair from the old nightclub days is revived though it was off limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something taboo is prohibited by custom, banned from mention or practice.

clue.text: What cop might have on jerk kidnapping French #1

indicators.note: kidnapping means the twitch holds the French word inside it

parts.note: a tic is a jerking twitch
the French word for one, number one, is un

explanation.surface: A police officer's odd behaviour involves snatching France's top man.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman's uniform jacket is traditionally a tunic, the garment he wears.

clue.text: One tweeting a description of Boris Johnson?

definitions.meaning: a small garden songbird that twitters
blue for a Conservative, tit for a fool

explanation.surface: A dig at a Tory former prime minister posting online.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party and a tit is slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The small blue-and-yellow garden bird chirps, and blue Tory plus idiot fits the politician.

clue.text: Acting ever so odd, having had too much Coke?

indicators.note: acting up, the letters of ever so odd behave unruly and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone behaving very strangely after drinking too much cola.
explanation.walkthrough: Coke with a capital looks like the soft drink, but it is cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdose is to take a dangerous excess of a drug such as cocaine.

clue.text: Country dudes getting into operatic number

indicators.note: getting into means the word for dudes goes inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
dudes are men

explanation.surface: Guys singing a country-and-western piece within an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a nation in the Caucasus whose capital is Yerevan.

clue.text: Haircut 100 to prosecute 'grasping' Queen

parts.note: a ton is a hundred

indicators.note: grasping means the legal word holds the royal letter inside

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action against
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Eighties band Haircut 100 are taken to court by a greedy monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Haircut 100 was a British pop band; the split between 'Haircut' and '100' is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown worn by monks, a particular style of cut.

clue.text: Some terrific scenes recalled Star Wars?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the extracted letters are turned round
some of means only part of the run of letters is taken

explanation.surface: Someone remembers great moments from the space opera films.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Star Wars films are science fiction set in space.

clue.text: Devoted daughter out of head on drugs

indicators.note: the leading letter goes out, replaced by the letter for daughter

parts.note: someone on drugs is medicated

explanation.surface: A loyal daughter is off her head on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of head' swaps the first letter, M, for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone devoted to a cause or person is committed and loyal.

clue.text: Deconstruction jobs can create noise, I'm told

indicators.note: the words can make something new, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reports that demolition sites are noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm told' looks like a sound signal but is just part of the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking down buildings is the work of demolition, taking structures apart.

clue.text: Drop when flatulent emission circulates

indicators.note: circulates means going round, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: flatulence emits wind, or gas

explanation.surface: Something falls when wind goes round the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sag is to droop or sink downwards.

clue.text: New women's bra: an over-the-shoulder number?

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A lingerie advert for a novel bra worn over the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sam Browne is a military belt with a strap running diagonally over the shoulder; number means an item of clothing.

clue.text: Nuts? Mine are shot and they can't multiply

indicators.note: shot means ruined, so the letters are broken up and re-formed

explanation.surface: Someone says their mind is gone and they are bad at maths.
explanation.definitionFit: People lacking basic numeracy cannot do arithmetic such as multiplication.

clue.text: A function that a television's aerial aids?

definitions.meaning: an aerial helps a set pick up a clear signal

explanation.definitionFit: A formal welcoming party is one sense; picking up broadcast signals is the other.

clue.text: Sad to report trapped wind fruit had caused?

indicators.note: to report means the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: colic is painful trapped wind, and a melon is a fruit: melon colic

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy explains that fruit gave them painful wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: melancholic means gloomy, low in spirits.

clue.text: Liberal avoiding topless place where one can stay the night

definitions.text: place where one can stay the night

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: avoiding is dodging

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician shuns a topless establishment when seeking a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodging is accommodation, a room or house for staying overnight.

clue.text: What might be chewed and regularly clued

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Something chewed over, as a clue routinely is.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows chew the cud, food brought back up from the stomach.

clue.text: Horse-drawn carriage seen in The Boston Tea Party?

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
a riot is a wild party or a great time

explanation.surface: A carriage seen in a historic protest in colonial America.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boston Tea Party was a 1773 protest, itself a kind of riot; here 'Tea' and 'Party' each give a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled carriage pulled by horses, as in ancient racing.

clue.text: Top treatment for ruddy nodding dog!

parts.note: ruddy means red in complexion
a nodding dog is a toy dog on a car's rear shelf, a car pet

explanation.surface: A cheerful remark about a red toy dog bobbing its head.
explanation.walkthrough: A nodding dog is a toy dog whose head bobs, popular in British car rear windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-carpet treatment is the special welcome given to VIPs, the best possible hospitality.

clue.text: Sausage that bishop pulls out of raging passion?

indicators.note: pulls out of means the bishop's letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a banger is British slang for a sausage
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cheeky innuendo about a clergyman and a sausage in heated passion.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is everyday British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury or rage is a strong emotion, a fierce passion of wrath.

clue.text: Hymn that's on hand to entertain soprano

indicators.note: to entertain means to host, holding the singer's letter inside

parts.note: the palm is part of the hand

explanation.surface: A sacred song is ready to amuse a choir's soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms are sacred songs of the Bible, sung as hymns.

clue.text: Just married — it's a test people say

parts.note: an oral exam is a spoken test

explanation.surface: Newly-weds are told that wedding is a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: just and moral both describe what is right and fair.

clue.text: Husband punches footballer and he moans

indicators.note: the husband's letter punches into the footballer, landing inside

parts.note: a winger plays on the flank of a football team

explanation.surface: A husband hits a soccer player, who complains.
explanation.definitionFit: A whinger is someone who complains or grumbles constantly.

clue.text: Epitaph starts with 'Poorly? I'm really on the up!'

indicators.note: on the up means the letters read upwards in this down entry
starts means the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A sick person insists they are recovering, ironically on a tombstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation of Rest In Peace, the common inscription on gravestones.

clue.text: Famous old luvvie, one bottled by Reed?

indicators.note: bottled by means the actor's first name holds the letter inside it

parts.note: Oliver Reed was a hard-drinking English actor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A celebrated old actor gets hit with a bottle by fellow thespian Oliver Reed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottled' hints at Reed's drinking; luvvie is British slang for a theatrical actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a renowned British stage and film actor, a celebrated thespian.

clue.text: Up for it always if a bit of gin's involved

indicators.note: involved means the letters go inside the word for always

parts.note: e'er is a poetic form of ever, always

indicators.note: a bit means just the first letter of the drink

explanation.surface: Someone is always game if there's gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being up for it means keen or ready to do it.

clue.text: Job near city Brown rejected after Labour

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown is turned down for a post after the Labour government.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour with a capital suggests Britain's political party and Gordon Brown, its PM; it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Postnatal describes the period following childbirth, after labour.
